title: Ontogeny and function of plasmacytoid dendritic cells in JAK2-associated myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN)
summary:
This study focuses on a specific type of immune cell called plasmacytoid dendritic cells. These cells play an important role in the body’s defense against infections, particularly by producing signaling molecules that regulate inflammation. However, it is still not fully understood how these cells develop and how their activity is controlled.

Patients with certain blood disorders known as myeloproliferative neoplasms often carry a genetic change in the JAK2 gene. This mutation provides a unique opportunity to trace the origin and function of immune cells. In this study, blood samples from affected patients and from healthy volunteers are analyzed to better understand where these immune cells come from and how they work. The study also examines how an established treatment with interferon influences the function of these cells. Overall, the goal is to gain fundamental insights into the immune system that may improve our understanding of blood and immune diseases in the future.

interventions.name: Recruitment and blood collection of patients with JAK2-associated myeloproliferative neoplasms and healthy volunteers. Molecular, genetic, and cellular characterization of plasmacytoid dendritic cells.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Eligible participants include adult patients with a diagnosed myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN) and a confirmed somatic JAK2 gain-of-function mutation, for example the V617F mutation, who are capable of providing informed consent. Samples will preferably be obtained in the context of routinely performed therapeutic phlebotomies. If no phlebotomy is scheduled, an alternative venous blood draw of up to 100 mL may be performed, provided that this is considered compatible with the patient’s health status by the treating physician. This upper limit is based on international recommendations, including the WHO Guidelines on Drawing Blood (2010).

In addition, healthy adult, non-pregnant control individuals will be recruited who, after appropriate information and written informed consent, agree to a single blood draw of approximately 50 mL.
Exclusion criteria:
Excluded from participation are minors and individuals who are not capable of providing informed consent, patients with additional hematologic or solid malignancies (other than MPN), individuals with acute infections at the time of sample collection, and individuals receiving immunosuppressive medication (with the exception of PEG-interferon). Pregnancy and breastfeeding are also exclusion criteria.
